title: feat: add Azure TTS models to speech routes
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds `openai/tts-1` and `openai/tts-1-hd` to the existing speech endpoints using Azure and Quest Pollen; preserves the ElevenLabs aliases.
- Uses Azure's published $15/$30 per million-character rates with multiplier 1; adds explicit pricing expectations and snapshots.
- Verified 24 live local E2E cases across both endpoints, both models, six voices and six formats, plus cache and disconnect/rejoin checks. Wallet deductions and staging Tinybird agree: 28 generations, 0.0333 Quest Pollen, no duplicate charges.
- Validation: 177 focused Gen tests, Gen typecheck, and 479 Enter pricing/alias tests passed. Required CI reruns on the latest commit.
- Azure deployments now serve speech successfully. Each still has 1 RPM allocated against its separate 3 RPM regional quota. Azure character/cost metrics and today's Cost Management records contain no TTS billing quantities yet; provider-side billing reconciliation remains unverified.

gist.headline: The hive finds its voice
gist.blurb: Two Azure-backed voices have joined the speech routes: `openai/tts-1` and `openai/tts-1-hd`. The ElevenLabs aliases are still right where you left them.
gist.summary: Added Azure-backed `openai/tts-1` and `openai/tts-1-hd` to both existing speech endpoints, with Quest Pollen pricing based on $15 and $30 per million characters respectively, while preserving ElevenLabs aliases.
gist.impact: Developers can request either new model through the existing speech routes; live checks covered six voices, six formats, caching, and disconnect/rejoin without duplicate wallet charges.
